meta.title: Improving Ergonomic Problems in my room
header_left: American University of the Middle East

background: AUM started online classes from March, and I spend most of the time in my study room.
Sitting for more than 12 hours makes me very exhausted, and I need to identify and improve ergonomic problems.
Coronavirus pandemic may continue next 1-2 years (source)
I want to resolve my problems in my study room.

items: I sit with bad posture for long hours.
I get tired after sitting 2 hours.

goals: Make a feasible implementation / deployment plan

steps: Because it takes time to find
Because I want to see PC screen clearly

steps.text: I did not change the PC settings

notes: We can evaluate the progress by measuring time to find iPhone, keys, wallet, and staples.
Evaluate the progress by a subjective feeling of neck-pain

blocks.heading: A. Used Ergonomics checklist (“Search”) for Item lost and messy desk problems
points: Perhaps labels or color could be utilized?
Will better layout of the workstation eliminate searching?
Can tools and parts be prepositioned?

blocks.heading: B. Used the Ergonomics checklist (“General posture evaluation, computer workstation) for the neck-pain, tiresome, and bad posture problems.
points: Are the joints maintained in a neutral position? (most are straight, elbow is at 90)
Has the chair been adjusted first, then keyboard and mouse, finally the monitor?
Is the monitor positioned 16 to 30 inches (roughly arm’s length) from the eyes?
Is the document holder utilized for data transfer from papers?
Are static postures avoided? i.e., are there changes in posture?

blocks.heading: Solutions for the search/messy (I, V) problems
points: Change the layout of the workstation
Buy a light-stand, small containers, and bookshelf
Make preposition (home-position) for tools and put them back after using them.
Make a routine time for organizing and cleaning every day for 5 minutes

blocks.heading: Solutions for the bad posture, neck pain and tiresome (II, III, and IV) problems.
points: Adjust the chair, then keyboard, mouse, and finally monitor so that joints maintain in a neutral position.
Position the monitor 16 30 inches (roughly arm’s length) from my eyes.
Avoid static postures, and make time for stretching and back-muscle exercising
Conduct stretch and exercise the back muscle

bullets: It is assumed to use items for 10 years to 30 years (my children can also use them)
Hours in a year = 4 hours/day x 7 days/week x 50 weeks/year = 1400 hours/year
The total cost per hour was 0.002KD/h, and it is acceptable for me.
If I spend one more year to graduate, it costs more than 418KD, this is acceptable.
